headline: GAP-183 (PID reuse) is genuinely closed live; GAP-175/176/177/178 hold; but GAP-184's fix is bypassable with a trivially adjusted forgery, and GAP-185's fix is incomplete: a state.json whose READ throws (EBUSY) is silently dropped and GC kills a live, reachable, default-state-root session and deletes its profile (real run, exit 0).

newGaps.GAP-188: major -- GAP-185 incomplete: read-error (EBUSY/EACCES) on state.json drops the session instead of marking it unreadable; live session killed + profile deleted (gap185-locked-state*.json)
newGaps.GAP-189: major -- GAP-184 bypass: plain node carrier + --user-data-dir=<tempRoot>\sutradhar-cli-* + file renamed state.json reproduces all 3 audit-2 effects (gap184-bypass.json)
newGaps.GAP-190: minor, test-integrity -- GAP-183's actual ordering comparison has no test (N1 survives 156/156; the 'PID-reuse' unit test is vacuous: nobody's ppid is the killed browser); N2, N4 also survive
newGaps.GAP-191: minor -- persistently-corrupt state.json protects its orphan Chrome forever with no age-based reclaim and no recovery hint (recovers only via next CLI command in that cwd)
newGaps.GAP-192: observation -- CLI readState-mid-write -> spawnFreshSession leaks a Chrome per concurrent command (74 profiles / ~6.1 GB in one 200s run); plausible root cause of GAP-187; pre-dates FR2-03

doneWhen: donewhen-run1-* (first attempt 21/24: 3 harness-expectation failures, explained in report)
